R.E.A.C.H. Development Strategy

Building on the previous R.I.S.E. framework, UM will implement the R.E.A.C.H. strategy to advance the cross-border ‘One University, Two Campuses’ model and move towards becoming a ‘first-class university in China with world excellence’.

R — Resource-integrated: Strengthen cross-border coordination in teaching and research, integrate disciplines and resources, and develop a unified operating model.
E — Excellence-focused: Pursue excellence in education, research, international cooperation, social service and institutional governance.
A — Ambition-led: Strengthen UM's leadership in Macao's higher education sector, Macao–Hengqin integration and Greater Bay Area development.
C — Collaboration-centric: Draw on international networks to attract academic resources and promote collaboration with society and industry.
H — High-impact: Generate valuable education and research outcomes, contribute to major societal needs and raise UM's international academic influence.
4S • 4 Zones • 4 Aims

UM will pursue internationalisation through the ‘4S • 4 Zones • 4 Aims’ framework, strengthening the quality of its programmes, student intake, academic staff and collaborative initiatives.

4S Strategy: Strategic, Substantial, Specific and Sustainable.

4 Zones: Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries; English-speaking countries; countries along the Belt and Road and neighbouring Asia-Pacific countries; and the Chinese Mainland and the Hong Kong SAR, including C9+ institutions and other top universities.

4 Aims: International faculty members, internationalised programmes, international students and international exchange.

The overall objective is to establish UM as an internationally oriented, collaborative and dynamic hub for teaching and research.
Global Partnership Network

UM aims to develop a high-quality global partnership network spanning more than 400 partner institutions across over 40 countries and regions. The strategy emphasises not only the geographic reach of partnerships but also deeper academic collaboration, international student recruitment and greater global visibility.

The University will review prospective and existing partners in a structured manner, prioritising institutions with strong academic reputations, complementary disciplinary strengths and a clear willingness to cooperate. It will develop regular channels for communication and coordination at the university, faculty and disciplinary levels.
Four Priority Regions

Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries: UM will reinforce links with institutions in Portugal, including the University of Lisbon, the University of Coimbra, the University of Porto, the University of Minho and NOVA University Lisbon. It will also engage institutions in Brazil, Mozambique and Angola, and seek new partnerships in Spain and South America.

English-speaking countries: UM will consolidate cooperation with institutions in the UK, Australia, Singapore, Canada and New Zealand.

Belt and Road and neighbouring Asia-Pacific countries: Priority markets include Vietnam, Malaysia and South Korea.

Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong SAR: UM will upgrade strategic partnerships with C9+ members and other leading institutions, developing regular and multi-level mechanisms for engagement.
International Programmes Across Academic Units

UM aims for each faculty, institute and residential college to offer international programmes. The University will move beyond establishing institutional links by developing substantive dual degree programmes, joint education, collaborative research and academic exchange opportunities.

On the Cooperation Zone campus, particular attention will be given to international collaboration involving the Faculty of Medicine, Faculty of Information Science and Computing, Faculty of Engineering and Faculty of Design. Partners will be selected on the basis of their academic standing, disciplinary complementarity and willingness to pursue workable cooperation.
International Dual Degrees and Joint Education

UM plans to develop international programmes involving several academic units on the Cooperation Zone campus. The Faculty of Medicine will work with the University of Lisbon in Portugal to jointly offer a clinical medicine programme. The Faculty of Information Science and Computing, Faculty of Engineering and Faculty of Design plan to establish dual degree programmes with the University of Barcelona in Spain, the University of Wollongong in Australia and Brunel University of London in the UK, respectively.

UM will also cooperate with Conde S. Januário Hospital and the Macao Medical Center of Peking Union Medical College Hospital in developing a teaching hospital, and will continue to explore collaborative education with renowned universities in other disciplines.
Research Collaboration and the China–Lusophone–Hispanophone Platform

UM will strengthen Macao's role as a platform linking China with Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries in science, technology and education. A key initiative is the proposed Centre for Ocean Research between China and Portuguese-speaking Countries.

Cooperation with institutions such as the University of Lisbon and the University of Coimbra will focus on distinctive strengths, including Chinese medicine, humanities and social sciences, language and cultural studies. With members of the C9+ League and other leading institutions in the Chinese Mainland, UM will explore joint research centres, laboratories and major collaborative research projects.
University Alliances and Exchange Organisations

UM will deepen its participation in university alliances and associations as a means of supporting research cooperation, academic seminars, cultural exchange and staff and student mobility.

The plan highlights Erasmus+, the Association of Portuguese Language Universities (AULP) and the International Association for the Exchange of Students for Technical Experience (IAESTE) as channels for engagement with institutions in the European Union, Portuguese-speaking countries and other regions.

UM will also participate in regional alliances such as the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao University Alliance, the alliance for technology, innovation and talent development in the western Greater Bay Area, and the Jiangsu–Hong Kong–Macao and Shandong–Hong Kong–Macao university collaboration networks.
Exchanges with Leading Universities

UM will continue to participate in programmes such as the Harvard-Yenching Institute Visiting Scholars Programme, the Clare Hall Visiting Fellowship Programme at the University of Cambridge, and international exchange activities associated with Oriel College at the University of Oxford.

The University will encourage outstanding students to undertake short-term study visits and exchanges at leading institutions in the Chinese Mainland and overseas, including participation in research projects and academic activities. It will also expand summer camps and short-term academic training programmes, attracting students from international partner institutions to UM and developing sustained academic and people-to-people connections.
International Conferences and Flagship Academic Events

UM will attract internationally recognised flagship conferences and academic events and co-host activities with partner institutions. Faculties and research institutes will be encouraged to organise annual conferences and thematic series of international academic forums to connect with high-calibre global academic resources and increase the University's international visibility.

The plan also calls for closer alignment with leading international curricula, teaching practices and assessment standards. Priority areas for curriculum enhancement include data science, artificial intelligence, pharmacy and health sciences.
International Recruitment and Scholarships

UM will strengthen incentives, streamline administration and improve support for international student recruitment. It plans categorised scholarship arrangements — Categories A, B and C — for international master's students, covering key expenses such as tuition and living costs. Additional financial support will be made available for international students taking part in semester exchanges and summer programmes at UM.

The University also intends to streamline internal procedures for exchange programmes and international recruitment, and to restructure the university-level admissions committee to improve coordination among relevant functional units and the efficiency of decision-making.
Joint-Programme Student Support and Partnership Outcomes

UM will strengthen whole-process management of students in joint education programmes with partner institutions in the Chinese Mainland and Portuguese-, Spanish- and English-speaking countries.

Support measures will cover cross-university credit transfer, student record management, accommodation and cultural orientation. A feedback and evaluation mechanism will review the effectiveness of partnerships and monitor the progress of dual degree programmes, research projects and academic exchange activities. Findings from these reviews will be used to refine cooperation strategies and student services.
Internationalisation of Postgraduate Education

UM aims to advance postgraduate education through global engagement, educational excellence and stronger quality assurance, with particular emphasis on expanding international student recruitment for master's programmes.

Recruitment measures include recommendation mechanisms with leading institutions in the Chinese Mainland, targeted publicity for selected institutions and programmes, outreach in Asian markets such as Malaysia and Vietnam, participation in international education fairs, dual degree and exchange opportunities, and more experience-based recruitment events.

In doctoral education, the University plans to introduce translational research into PhD curricula, establish a university-level doctoral research exchange programme and upgrade its digital postgraduate management arrangements.
Student Population in 2030/31

The five-year plan projects a total student population of 22,211 in the academic year 2030/31, including 9,887 undergraduates and 12,324 postgraduates. Postgraduates are expected to account for approximately 55 per cent of all students.

By campus, the projection is 18,244 students on the Macao main campus and 3,967 on the Cooperation Zone campus. The main-campus figure includes approximately 2,000 students who will attend classes and undertake research on both campuses. The plan also envisages a 1:1 ratio between humanities and social sciences students and science, engineering and medicine students.

A longer-term institutional goal is to reach 25,000 students by 2035.
Residential Colleges and Postgraduate Colleges

UM plans to expand its residential college network to 20 colleges across two campuses, comprising 14 undergraduate and six postgraduate colleges. The main campus is expected to have 12 colleges and the Cooperation Zone campus eight, including three postgraduate colleges on each campus.

The proposed postgraduate colleges will be developed around the themes ‘Innovation and Interdisciplinary Exchange’, ‘Research Excellence’ and ‘Global Engagement’. They will serve groups including doctoral researchers, international and exchange students, and students from relevant research institutes. Core curriculum modules and signature activities will support research, innovation, internationalisation and student development.
Hengqin Campus and One University, Two Campuses

The new Cooperation Zone campus is projected to begin partial operations in 2028, be fully completed in 2029 and enter a phase of expansion and refinement in 2030. This construction timetable is distinct from the existing first-phase arrangements already supporting cross-border teaching.

UM will implement an integrated ‘One University, Two Campuses’ management model, ensuring consistency in institutional governance, operations, student education and academic qualifications while complying with the legal requirements of both jurisdictions.

A management committee and operational entity will be established in the Cooperation Zone, with corresponding offices of main-campus functional units supporting integrated operations.
N.E.T. Research Strategy

UM will move beyond its earlier ‘Four Threes’ research structure by adopting the N.E.T. strategy, integrating interdisciplinary research and an ‘AI+’ approach.

N — Nurturing Cores: Strengthen the three State Key Laboratories in Chinese Medicine, Microelectronics and Internet of Things for Smart City, developing a coordinated ‘Laboratory + Research Institute’ structure.

E — Enabling Ecosystem: Develop research clusters and platforms in artificial intelligence and brain sciences, biomedical sciences and clinical translation, intelligent medical engineering, and energy and carbon neutrality.

T — Threading Networks: Link research capabilities across the two campuses with the needs of industries and markets in the Greater Bay Area, creating an open regional innovation network.
Cross-Border Data and Digital Administration

UM will develop dedicated network connections between its campuses, enhance secure access to international internet and research networks, and establish trusted mechanisms for cross-border data exchange.

The plan includes phased upgrades to the University's core information systems, the intelligent development of the UM App and implementation of the UM Flow office automation platform to strengthen cross-departmental coordination.

Priority will also be given to a transcript verification service for postgraduate admission applications, including authentication via the China Higher Education Student Information system and mutual recognition among Greater Bay Area institutions. Cross-border data security assessments and emergency response mechanisms will accompany these initiatives.
Sustainable Development Goals and International Cooperation

UM will incorporate the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into its overall strategy and consider establishing a university-level sustainability body to coordinate education, research, campus management, public services and international cooperation.

Research priorities include human health and well-being, smart city development and environmental protection. In partnership with governments, enterprises, international organisations and global alliances, UM will promote sustainable development, green campus initiatives, ESG governance and broader social responsibility. Cross-border collaboration between Macao and Hengqin forms part of this approach.
